Name: Huly
Short_Description: All-in-one process, project, time and knowledge environment with a central team calendar. The hosted service closed in July 2026; self-hosting continues.
Community_Proxy_Evidence: 27.7k stars and 2.2k forks, on a long commit history.
GitHub_Stars_Caveat: hcengineering/platform is the whole platform — tracker, documents, calendar and messaging. No repository counts Huly the task manager on its own.
Integration_Notes: GitHub synchronisation is the notable one. The surface is smaller than Plane’s or OpenProject’s.
Deployment: Docker Compose across several services, with MongoDB or CockroachDB, object storage and a search index. The heaviest stack here.
Calendar_Sync: A built-in team calendar, but no CalDAV or iCalendar interface to it.
Data_Out: Workspace backup and restore tooling, plus a plugin and API surface; not recorded as a set of named export formats.
Stack: TypeScript and Svelte over MongoDB or CockroachDB.
Hosted_Option: None recorded. The first-party hosted service closed in July 2026; self-hosting continues.
Ease_of_Deployment_Review: The most components to stand up of anything here, and the most to keep running.
Ease_of_Use_Review: One integrated workspace, wide enough that finding your way takes a while.
Enterprise_Features_Review: The collaboration and process breadth is real. Continuity and the support model are the question.
Interface_Flexibility_Review: Projects, messaging, calendar and documents in one interface.
Data_Sovereignty_Review: EPL source and self-hosting, untouched by the hosted service closing.
Portability_Review: Open source, but so broad that replacing it means replacing several tools at once.
Activity_or_Caveat: The hosted service was announced for shutdown around 20 Jul 2026. Self-hosting was stated to be unaffected.

Name: OpenProject
Short_Description: Classic, agile and hybrid project portfolio management with work packages, boards, Gantt, and native time and cost tracking.
Community_Proxy_Evidence: A maintained Community Edition, documentation, forums and regular releases. Integration work continued in Sep 2026.
Integration_Notes: GitHub, GitLab, Nextcloud, OneDrive, SharePoint and XWiki are named, with a REST API for the rest.
Deployment: A packaged all-in-one container, distribution packages, or an official Helm chart over PostgreSQL.
Calendar_Sync: iCalendar subscription URLs per work-package view, one way out. No CalDAV.
Data_Out: CSV, XLSX and PDF exports; REST APIv3 with OAuth2.
Stack: Ruby on Rails and Angular over PostgreSQL.
Ease_of_Deployment_Review: Packages, containers and an official Helm chart, carrying a heavier stack than minimalist tools.
Ease_of_Use_Review: Capable and clear, but the PM vocabulary and configuration depth take time to learn.
Enterprise_Features_Review: Permissions, identity, audit, portfolio reporting, and cost and time management, all native.
Interface_Flexibility_Review: Tables, boards, Gantt, calendars, filters, custom workflows and per-project modules.
Data_Sovereignty_Review: The Community Edition can be self-hosted, with GPL-licensed source and control over the database.
Portability_Review: A conventional stack with API and export routes out. Some advanced functions are edition-bound.
Activity_or_Caveat: Check each feature against the Community Edition. Much of what is advertised is Enterprise.

Name: Plane
Short_Description: Product-development workspace built on work items, cycles, modules and initiatives, with the widest advertised integration surface here.
Community_Proxy_Evidence: High GitHub visibility, with docs and product pages updated in Sep 2026.
Integration_Notes: Slack, GitHub and Figma among the advertised connections, plus APIs, webhooks, OAuth apps and MCP.
Deployment: Docker Compose over PostgreSQL, Redis and MinIO object storage, or a Kubernetes chart. Several services, not one container.
Calendar_Sync: None. Neither CalDAV nor an iCalendar feed.
Data_Out: CSV and JSON exports of work items; REST API, webhooks, OAuth apps and MCP.
Stack: Next.js and TypeScript over Python (Django) and PostgreSQL.
Hosted_Option: First-party (Plane Cloud), alongside the self-hosted Community Edition.
Ease_of_Deployment_Review: Documented Docker and Kubernetes paths, with more moving parts than a single-container app.
Ease_of_Use_Review: Teams arriving from Linear or Jira need almost no reorientation.
Enterprise_Features_Review: Governance and deployment options run deep, though several sit outside the AGPL Community tier.
Interface_Flexibility_Review: Board, spreadsheet, list and Gantt views, over configurable work items, cycles and initiatives.
Data_Sovereignty_Review: Open Community code, deployable on-prem and air-gapped. The tier boundary is the limit.
Portability_Review: APIs and webhooks are there, but open-core splits make a like-for-like exit harder.
Activity_or_Caveat: Open core. Do not assume a feature on the marketing site is in the Community Edition.

Name: Redmine
Short_Description: Two decades of configurable issue workflows, custom fields, multiple databases and a vast plugin ecosystem. Dated interface, exceptional survivability.
Community_Proxy_Evidence: Nearly two decades of continuity, busy forums and plugins, and several supported-version releases in Aug 2026.
GitHub_Stars_Caveat: GitHub carries a read-only mirror. Development lives in the project’s own repository at redmine.org, so this figure sits far below two decades of installed base.
Integration_Notes: A large plugin ecosystem and a REST API. Agile boards usually arrive as a plugin, not from core.
Deployment: An official Docker image or distribution packages over PostgreSQL, MySQL or SQLite. Conventional and well documented.
Calendar_Sync: iCalendar and Atom feeds over issue queries, one way out. No CalDAV.
Data_Out: CSV, PDF, XML and JSON exports; a full REST API in XML and JSON.
Stack: Ruby on Rails over PostgreSQL, MySQL or SQLite.
Hosted_Option: Third-party only (Planio, Easy Redmine and others); no first-party service.
Ease_of_Deployment_Review: Well understood, but the Ruby stack, plugins and upgrades want an admin who knows them.
Ease_of_Use_Review: It works, and it looks its age. The configuration depth overwhelms casual users.
Enterprise_Features_Review: Workflows, roles, custom fields and multi-project operation, extended by twenty years of plugins.
Interface_Flexibility_Review: Almost any workflow or field can be configured, behind an old-fashioned interface.
Data_Sovereignty_Review: GPL, self-hosted, and it runs on the database you already have.
Portability_Review: A REST API, standard databases, and two decades of continuity to archive against.
Activity_or_Caveat: The weakness is the interface, not the project’s health. Three supported versions shipped in Aug 2026.

Name: AFFiNE
Short_Description: Documents, an infinite whiteboard and databases in one workspace, with tasks as database views rather than a tracker of their own.
Community_Proxy_Evidence: 72.7k GitHub stars and frequent releases; a large audience for the editor, a much smaller one running the backend themselves.
Integration_Notes: A GraphQL API with WebSocket sync, and built-in AI. Packaged connections to other task systems are thin.
Deployment: Documented Docker Compose with PostgreSQL and Redis, or the hosted service.
Calendar_Sync: None. Neither CalDAV nor an iCalendar feed.
Data_Out: Markdown, HTML, JSON and PDF or PNG exports; a GraphQL API with WebSocket sync.
Hosted_Option: First-party (AFFiNE Cloud), plus a paid self-hosted Team tier.
Ease_of_Deployment_Review: Documented Docker Compose with PostgreSQL and Redis. More moving parts than a notes app suggests.
Ease_of_Use_Review: One of the most polished interfaces in this table, and the whiteboard has no real peer here.
Enterprise_Features_Review: Multi-admin roles and team management sit in the paid self-hosted tier, not in the free build.
Interface_Flexibility_Review: Docs, edgeless whiteboard and database views over the same content, freely mixed.
Data_Sovereignty_Review: The client is open; the self-hosted backend is under an Enterprise Edition licence. That is the ceiling.
Portability_Review: Markdown, HTML, JSON and PDF out over GraphQL. Fine for documents, thinner for structured work.
Activity_or_Caveat: The client is open and the self-hosted backend is not: it ships under an AFFiNE Enterprise Edition licence, and administrative features sit behind the paid Team tier. Self-hosted and open source are two different claims here, and this is the clearest case in the table of why the distinction matters.

Name: AppFlowy
Short_Description: A Notion-shaped workspace of nested documents and inline databases, where board, table and calendar are three views of the same records.
Community_Proxy_Evidence: 76.8k GitHub stars and active releases through 2026, with a following much larger than the self-hosted share of it.
Integration_Notes: A self-hosted cloud sync server, local and hosted language models, and a cloud API. Packaged connectors to other task systems are limited.
Deployment: Compose for the self-hosted AppFlowy Cloud sync server; the web client sits alongside desktop and mobile builds.
Calendar_Sync: None. Neither CalDAV nor an iCalendar feed.
Data_Out: JSON, Markdown and CSV exports; a cloud API with WebSocket sync.
Hosted_Option: First-party (AppFlowy Cloud), with paid AI and vault add-ons.
Ease_of_Deployment_Review: Compose for the self-hosted sync server, with several services behind it. Documented, but not a single container.
Ease_of_Use_Review: Polished and immediately familiar to anyone who has used Notion.
Enterprise_Features_Review: Workspace roles and guest links. SSO, audit and the vault tier are paid.
Interface_Flexibility_Review: Table, board, calendar and nested documents over configurable database fields.
Data_Sovereignty_Review: The AGPL workspace self-hosts, though the AI and vault tiers are where the vendor keeps its margin.
Portability_Review: JSON, Markdown and CSV out, over a cloud API. Adequate rather than generous.
Activity_or_Caveat: Open core, and the desktop and mobile clients lead the web one. Check that the capability you need is in the AGPL build rather than in an AI or vault tier before committing.

Name: Habitica
Short_Description: Habits, dailies and to-dos wrapped in a role-playing game, where parties and guilds carry the accountability a manager otherwise would.
Community_Proxy_Evidence: 14.2k GitHub stars against a very large hosted player base, an active wiki and a long list of third-party apps.
Integration_Notes: API v3 with user-configurable webhooks, a documented third-party application list, and connectors through Make and similar automation platforms.
Deployment: Compose with Node.js, MongoDB and Redis.
Calendar_Sync: None. Neither CalDAV nor an iCalendar feed.
Data_Out: JSON and CSV exports; a full REST API with user-configurable webhooks.
Hosted_Option: First-party (habitica.com), where nearly all of its users are.
Ease_of_Deployment_Review: Compose with Node.js, MongoDB and Redis. Possible to self-host, but the hosted service is the trodden path.
Ease_of_Use_Review: Genuinely enjoyable for the people it suits, and completely alien to anyone wanting a project tool.
Enterprise_Features_Review: Parties, guilds and challenge managers. A social structure, not an organisational one.
Interface_Flexibility_Review: Four fixed list types and no views at all. The narrowest interface in this table.
Data_Sovereignty_Review: GPLv3 and self-hostable in full; the subscriptions are cosmetic and live on the hosted service.
Portability_Review: JSON and CSV exports over a full REST API, which is more than the category usually offers.
Activity_or_Caveat: A motivation system rather than a project tool. There is no board, timeline or calendar, and the self-hosted path is far less travelled than habitica.com — expect to be an early reader of your own logs.

Name: Leantime
Short_Description: Project management aimed at non-project-managers: tasks, Kanban, timelines, retrospectives, strategy boards and native timesheets.
Community_Proxy_Evidence: Large GitHub following, a running marketplace and community chat, and continuing development.
Integration_Notes: A marketplace and an API widen the coverage. The count moves as the marketplace does.
Deployment: Docker Compose with PHP, a web server and MySQL. One database, no queue or object store.
Calendar_Sync: iCalendar feed URLs for tasks and milestones, one way out. No CalDAV.
Data_Out: CSV and JSON exports, plus timesheet exports; REST API and webhooks.
Stack: PHP over MySQL, with a server-rendered interface.
Ease_of_Deployment_Review: A standard web stack with container options. Plugin management adds ongoing upkeep.
Ease_of_Use_Review: Built for teams with no project manager in them, and it shows.
Enterprise_Features_Review: The organisational features are real, but governance and portfolio administration stop short of OpenProject.
Interface_Flexibility_Review: Task views, timelines, retrospectives and strategy boards, extensible past them.
Data_Sovereignty_Review: The AGPL core self-hosts, so deployment and data stay yours.
Portability_Review: The core and its API leave cleanly. Anything running on a paid plugin needs replacing first.
Activity_or_Caveat: The core is open. Advanced functionality may arrive as a paid plugin.

Name: Logseq
Short_Description: An outliner over plain Markdown and Org-mode files, where the task list is a query across notes you already wrote.
Community_Proxy_Evidence: 45.0k GitHub stars and 486 plugins in the marketplace as of August 2026, against a database rewrite that has been in beta a long time.
Integration_Notes: 486 marketplace plugins as of August 2026, most of them editor extensions rather than connections to other systems, plus Git-based sync over the files themselves.
Deployment: A self-hosted web app container, a desktop build, or the hosted browser demo reading a local folder.
Calendar_Sync: None. Neither CalDAV nor an iCalendar feed.
Data_Out: The files are the export: Markdown and Org-mode on disk, plus JSON; a plugin API.
Stack: ClojureScript and React over plain text files.
Hosted_Option: None. The files stay yours, synced by whatever you already use.
Ease_of_Deployment_Review: A container for the self-hosted web app, or no server at all if you run the desktop build.
Ease_of_Use_Review: Outliner literacy is the entry fee. Once paid, querying tasks out of notes is unusually good.
Enterprise_Features_Review: Effectively single-user. There are no roles, no shared instance and no administration.
Interface_Flexibility_Review: Queries, references and 486 plugins will bend it to most shapes, given patience.
Data_Sovereignty_Review: Plain files on your own disk. Nothing scores higher than that, and nothing can.
Portability_Review: The files are the export. Markdown and Org-mode, readable without Logseq ever running again.
Activity_or_Caveat: The browser build depends on the File System Access API, so a local graph opens in Chromium only — Firefox and Safari cannot. The database rewrite has been in beta for a long time and plugin compatibility with it is still unsettled.

Name: Nextcloud Deck
Short_Description: Kanban inside Nextcloud, worth testing before deploying a second platform if Nextcloud is already in place.
Community_Proxy_Evidence: Carried by the far larger Nextcloud ecosystem, app store and install base. Deck is established within it.
GitHub_Stars_Caveat: The Deck app repository alone. Nextcloud, the platform Deck runs inside and inherits its install base from, holds about 36.8k of its own.
Integration_Notes: The value is in Nextcloud itself, Files and Calendar and sharing, rather than standalone connectors.
Deployment: The Nextcloud all-in-one container or distribution packages over PostgreSQL or MariaDB, then Deck and Tasks as apps.
Calendar_Sync: Native CalDAV through Nextcloud Tasks, read and write. The strongest phone and desktop story in the table.
Data_Out: iCalendar and CalDAV, JSON, and CSV through companion apps; OCS and REST APIs with webhooks.
Stack: PHP and Vue over PostgreSQL or MariaDB.
Hosted_Option: Third-party providers under the Nextcloud provider programme.
Ease_of_Deployment_Review: Trivial if Nextcloud is already running. Disproportionate if it is not.
Ease_of_Use_Review: A board and little else, in a place Nextcloud users already work.
Enterprise_Features_Review: Identity, sharing and administration are inherited from Nextcloud itself.
Interface_Flexibility_Review: Kanban, Gantt, and the surrounding Nextcloud apps. As standalone PM, shallow.
Data_Sovereignty_Review: AGPL, self-hosted, sitting alongside the rest of your files.
Portability_Review: A standards-friendly platform, though Deck data leaves only with Nextcloud.
Activity_or_Caveat: Comparisons saying Deck has no Gantt predate the Jun 2026 announcement.

Name: NocoDB
Short_Description: Puts grid, kanban, gallery, form and calendar views over a SQL database you already own, so the task board is a view rather than a new system of record.
Community_Proxy_Evidence: 65.0k GitHub stars with frequent releases, and wide deployment as a self-hosted Airtable replacement.
Integration_Notes: An auto-generated REST API with Swagger, per-table webhooks, native connectors to external PostgreSQL and MySQL sources, and packaged Zapier, n8n and Make apps.
Deployment: One container over SQLite, or pointed at an existing PostgreSQL or MySQL database.
Calendar_Sync: None. Neither CalDAV nor an iCalendar feed.
Data_Out: CSV, JSON and Excel exports; an auto-generated Swagger REST API, and per-table webhooks.
Stack: Node.js and Vue over SQLite, PostgreSQL or MySQL.
Ease_of_Deployment_Review: A single container over SQLite, or pointed straight at a database you already run.
Ease_of_Use_Review: Anyone who has used a spreadsheet is productive in minutes; the relational parts take longer.
Enterprise_Features_Review: Owner, creator, editor, commenter and viewer per base. SSO, audit and row-level policy are paid.
Interface_Flexibility_Review: Five view types over any table, with formulas, lookups, rollups and per-view filters.
Data_Sovereignty_Review: The AGPL core self-hosts in full; governance features are the part held back.
Portability_Review: Point it at your own PostgreSQL and the data never enters NocoDB's storage in the first place.
Activity_or_Caveat: A database with task views, not a task manager. There is no sprint, dependency or timeline unless you model one, and nothing stops a team modelling it badly.

Name: PLANKA
License: Edition-dependent; not treated here as pure OSI FOSS
Short_Description: Board-first Trello alternative. The Community edition is capable; timeline and calendar sit in the paid tiers.
Community_Proxy_Evidence: Widely visible in self-hosting circles and broadly used, on an official Community and Pro split.
Integration_Notes: A wide notification surface. That is not the same as a hundred two-way business integrations.
Deployment: A two-container Compose file: the application and PostgreSQL. Nothing else to run.
Calendar_Sync: None. Neither CalDAV nor an iCalendar feed.
Data_Out: JSON and CSV board exports; REST API and webhooks.
Hosted_Option: None recorded for the Community edition.
Ease_of_Deployment_Review: A compact container stack that comes up quickly.
Ease_of_Use_Review: The closest thing to Trello you can host yourself.
Enterprise_Features_Review: The business features exist, mostly in Pro and Enterprise rather than Community.
Interface_Flexibility_Review: The board is the product. The other views are thinner than a full suite’s.
Data_Sovereignty_Review: The data is yours. The licence and edition rules mean the software is not, entirely.
Portability_Review: You can move the instance. The fair-code terms still bind you where MIT and GPL peers would not.
Activity_or_Caveat: Read the licence before committing. Community is capable; several organisational features are paid.

Name: Taiga
Short_Description: Agile-first: backlogs, sprint boards, burndowns, WIP limits and swimlanes, with no native Gantt, calendar or time tracking.
Community_Proxy_Evidence: An established project with its own forum, documentation and years of agile-team adoption.
GitHub_Stars_Caveat: The codebase is split across taiga-docker, taiga-back and taiga-front. This is the largest of the three; the other two hold roughly 1.2k more between them.
Integration_Notes: Source-control and migration workflows. Community docs cover GitHub, GitLab, Gitea and Gogs.
Deployment: A multi-container Compose stack with an official install script, over PostgreSQL, RabbitMQ and Redis.
Calendar_Sync: None. Neither CalDAV nor an iCalendar feed.
Data_Out: A full project dump as JSON, plus CSV; comprehensive REST API and webhooks.
Ease_of_Deployment_Review: Documented well, but it is a multi-service stack rather than one container.
Ease_of_Use_Review: Immediately clear to a team that already runs sprints.
Enterprise_Features_Review: Agile workflow control is thorough. Portfolio, cost and governance are absent.
Interface_Flexibility_Review: Deep agile configuration and custom fields, with few of the classic PM views.
Data_Sovereignty_Review: Open source throughout, self-hosted in full.
Portability_Review: Open source, with importers, exports and an API to leave by.
Activity_or_Caveat: No native Gantt, calendar or time tracking. For some teams that ends the evaluation.

Name: Focalboard
Short_Description: Trello-shaped boards with table, gallery and calendar views over the same cards, from the Mattermost project and now maintained by whoever turns up.
Community_Proxy_Evidence: 26.5k GitHub stars from the Mattermost era, with community commits continuing into 2026 against an open call for maintainers.
Integration_Notes: A REST API and a board archive format. Deeper integration comes from running it inside Mattermost rather than from connectors of its own.
Deployment: A single Docker image for the personal server, or the board plugin inside Mattermost.
Calendar_Sync: None. Neither CalDAV nor an iCalendar feed.
Data_Out: JSON board archives and CSV exports; a REST API.
Hosted_Option: Through Mattermost Cloud, as part of that product rather than on its own.
Ease_of_Deployment_Review: A single Docker image for the personal server, or the board plugin inside an existing Mattermost.
Ease_of_Use_Review: Notion-style properties over a Trello-style board, and almost nothing to learn first.
Enterprise_Features_Review: Board-level roles only: admin, editor, commenter, viewer. No organisational model above that.
Interface_Flexibility_Review: Kanban, table, gallery and calendar over custom properties, with filters and grouping.
Data_Sovereignty_Review: MIT, self-hostable in full, and small enough to fork if it comes to that.
Portability_Review: JSON board archives and CSV, over a REST API. Enough to leave, not enough to automate around.
Activity_or_Caveat: Community-maintained. Mattermost stopped bundling the plugin in September 2023 and adds neither features nor fixes; commits continue from contributors against an open call for maintainers. Treat the roadmap as absent rather than slow.

Name: Grist
Short_Description: A relational spreadsheet with Python formulas and cell-level access rules, where the tracker is something you assemble rather than something you are given.
Community_Proxy_Evidence: 11.8k GitHub stars, steady releases, and visible adoption in public-sector and civic-tech deployments.
Integration_Notes: REST API with an interactive console, outgoing webhooks, custom widgets, and packaged Zapier, n8n and Make connectors.
Deployment: One official container over SQLite, with Python for formulas. No external database required.
Calendar_Sync: None. Neither CalDAV nor an iCalendar feed.
Data_Out: SQLite, CSV and Excel exports; REST API with an interactive console, and outgoing webhooks.
Hosted_Option: First-party (Grist hosted), with paid tiers above the Apache-2.0 core.
Ease_of_Deployment_Review: One official container over SQLite, with no queue, cache or object store to run beside it.
Ease_of_Use_Review: Spreadsheet fluency gets you a long way; a task board is still something you have to design.
Enterprise_Features_Review: Access rules down to the individual cell are the best in this table. SSO and SCIM are Enterprise.
Interface_Flexibility_Review: Widgets, Python formulas and linked views will model almost any process you can describe.
Data_Sovereignty_Review: grist-core self-hosts completely; the Enterprise build adds administration rather than function.
Portability_Review: Your document is a SQLite file. Few exits in this field are that clean.
Activity_or_Caveat: Not a task manager out of the box. You get a database, a formula language and the parts to build one, which is either exactly the point or immediately the problem.

Name: Kanboard
Short_Description: Deliberately minimal Kanban with SQLite by default, a plugin architecture, and almost no operational surface area.
Community_Proxy_Evidence: Long-lived, with 300+ contributors reported in project materials and a large plugin ecosystem.
Integration_Notes: Plugins, webhooks and an API. The working count changes over time.
Deployment: One PHP container over embedded SQLite, with PostgreSQL and MySQL optional. Almost no operational surface.
Calendar_Sync: iCalendar subscription feeds per project and per user, one way out. No CalDAV.
Data_Out: CSV and JSON exports; JSON-RPC API and webhooks.
Stack: PHP over SQLite by default; no build step and no JavaScript framework.
Ease_of_Deployment_Review: Runs on SQLite. There is almost nothing to operate.
Ease_of_Use_Review: Direct and unambiguous, and deliberately unpolished.
Enterprise_Features_Review: The workflow core is sound. Native governance and portfolio depth are not there.
Interface_Flexibility_Review: Swimlanes, automatic actions, Gantt, calendar and plugin hooks, behind a sparse interface that hides them.
Data_Sovereignty_Review: MIT, and small enough to read. Nothing constrains what you do with it.
Portability_Review: A permissive licence, an API and an ordinary database. Very little to leave behind.
Activity_or_Caveat: Suits teams that want simplicity and control more than a polished interface.

Name: Kimai
Short_Description: Timesheets first: activities, rates, budgets and invoices for teams whose tasks exist mainly to be billed.
Community_Proxy_Evidence: 5.0k GitHub stars, twenty years of continuity, frequent releases and an active official plugin store.
Integration_Notes: A JSON REST API, mobile and desktop clients, a CLI, and an official store carrying accounting and chat connectors such as Bexio, Lexoffice and Microsoft Teams.
Deployment: One Compose file with PHP, a web server and MySQL.
Calendar_Sync: An iCalendar feed of the timesheet, one way out. No CalDAV.
Data_Out: CSV, XLSX, PDF and JSON exports, plus invoice templates; a JSON REST API.
Ease_of_Deployment_Review: One Compose file with PHP and MySQL. A long-standing project with installation documentation to match.
Ease_of_Use_Review: The timesheet is the interface, and for its audience that is exactly right.
Enterprise_Features_Review: Customer, user, team-lead and admin roles with strict visibility gates, plus SSO and an audit trail.
Interface_Flexibility_Review: Deep in one direction and absent in every other: no boards, no timelines, no issue workflow.
Data_Sovereignty_Review: The AGPL core tracks, budgets and invoices without reaching for the store.
Portability_Review: CSV, XLSX, PDF and JSON out, with a REST API. Getting time into an accounting system is the design goal.
Activity_or_Caveat: Open core by plugin. The AGPL core bills and invoices on its own, but a good deal of the ecosystem, including several accounting connectors, sits in a paid store.

Name: Super Productivity
Short_Description: A personal task list with pomodoro timing and timeboxing that pulls its work items out of the trackers your team already runs.
Community_Proxy_Evidence: 22.1k GitHub stars and frequent releases, driven by one maintainer with a steady contributor stream.
Integration_Notes: Jira, Trello, GitHub, GitLab, Gitea, Forgejo, OpenProject, Linear, ClickUp, Azure DevOps, Google Calendar and CalDAV, each called directly from your own device with no middleware in between.
Deployment: No server at all: a browser app, with optional WebDAV, Dropbox or local-file sync.
Calendar_Sync: Reads tasks from a CalDAV server as an issue source, and a Google Calendar feed. It is not a CalDAV server itself.
Data_Out: JSON and CSV exports, plus whatever the sync target holds; integrations with other trackers rather than an API of its own.
Stack: TypeScript and Angular, storing to IndexedDB.
Ease_of_Deployment_Review: There is nothing to deploy. It runs in the browser, and sync is a WebDAV target or a file you already keep.
Ease_of_Use_Review: Opinionated and quick: pick a task, start the timer, and the timesheet writes itself.
Enterprise_Features_Review: There is no multi-user model at all — no roles, no shared instance, no administration.
Interface_Flexibility_Review: A list, a schedule and time logs. Depth is in the timer and the issue providers, not in views.
Data_Sovereignty_Review: Your device holds the data and the app calls each service directly. Nothing to take away from you.
Portability_Review: JSON and CSV out, plus whatever your sync target already holds as plain files.
Activity_or_Caveat: Single-user by design. There are no roles, no shared instance and no server to administer, which is either exactly right or immediately disqualifying.

Name: Taskwarrior
Short_Description: A command-line task manager with a tuneable urgency model; the browser arrives through third-party clients built on its sync protocol.
Community_Proxy_Evidence: 6.1k GitHub stars and twenty years of continuity, with a devoted command-line following and a small ecosystem of front-ends.
Integration_Notes: The documented TaskChampion sync protocol, a hook system, and third-party clients including WingTask and taskwarrior_web. There is no first-party web interface.
Deployment: A local task database, plus an optional TaskChampion sync server.
Calendar_Sync: None. Neither CalDAV nor an iCalendar feed.
Data_Out: JSON and the native task format; a CLI, a hook system and a documented sync protocol.
Ease_of_Deployment_Review: A local database and an optional sync server. The browser route needs a third party you also have to trust.
Ease_of_Use_Review: Extraordinary if you live in a terminal, and close to opaque if you do not.
Enterprise_Features_Review: No roles, no organisation, no shared project. It was never trying.
Interface_Flexibility_Review: Contexts, filters, urgency coefficients and custom reports. Deep, and entirely textual.
Data_Sovereignty_Review: MIT and local, minus the part where the best browser client is somebody else's hosted service.
Portability_Review: JSON and a documented format with twenty years of compatibility behind it.
Activity_or_Caveat: There is no first-party web interface. Browser access comes from third-party clients on the sync protocol, and the most polished of them is a commercial hosted service — so the browser route is real, but it is not the project's own and is not covered by the MIT licence above.

Name: Trilium Notes
Short_Description: A scriptable hierarchical note tree. A first-party task list is in development; today a to-do is a note carrying a label.
Community_Proxy_Evidence: 37.9k GitHub stars carried over from the original project, with TriliumNext shipping regular releases since the original was archived.
GitHub_Stars_Caveat: TriliumNext/Trilium is the renamed original repository, so the count carries the archived project’s following with it rather than starting again.
Integration_Notes: ETAPI, a token-authenticated REST interface, plus scripts that run inside notes. No packaged connectors to other task systems.
Deployment: One container with embedded SQLite; desktop clients sync to it.
Calendar_Sync: None. Neither CalDAV nor an iCalendar feed.
Data_Out: HTML and Markdown exports, and a full database ZIP; ETAPI token-authenticated REST.
Hosted_Option: None. A self-hosted server, or a local desktop application.
Ease_of_Deployment_Review: One container with embedded SQLite, with desktop clients syncing to it.
Ease_of_Use_Review: Excellent as a knowledge base. As a task manager it asks you to invent the convention first.
Enterprise_Features_Review: Single-tenant and password-protected. There is no concept of another user.
Interface_Flexibility_Review: Attributes, templates and in-note scripting will build almost anything, slowly.
Data_Sovereignty_Review: AGPL, self-hosted, embedded database, and the whole thing exports as one file.
Portability_Review: HTML, Markdown and a complete database ZIP, plus ETAPI. Leaving is a download.
Activity_or_Caveat: Barely a task manager yet. A first-party task list is in development; today a to-do list is a note with an #initTodo label and a community script behind it. The original zadam/trilium is archived — TriliumNext is the maintained continuation and the one recorded here.

Name: Vikunja
Short_Description: Lightweight, sovereignty-first task management with list, Kanban, Gantt and table views, CalDAV, and importers from the major SaaS tools.
Community_Proxy_Evidence: Releases through 2026, established documentation, and a plugin system still growing.
GitHub_Stars_Caveat: GitHub carries a mirror. The project develops on its own Gitea at code.vikunja.io, and the following there is not counted in this figure.
Integration_Notes: CalDAV, and importers from Todoist, Trello and Microsoft To Do. Plugins widen it further.
Deployment: A single Go binary, or a two-container Compose file over SQLite or PostgreSQL. The lightest server here.
Calendar_Sync: Native CalDAV, read and write, against the same tasks the interface shows.
Data_Out: Full account export as JSON and a ZIP of attachments; CalDAV, REST API and webhooks.
Stack: Go and Vue over SQLite, PostgreSQL or MySQL.
Ease_of_Deployment_Review: Docker, or one native binary. Nothing else to stand up.
Ease_of_Use_Review: Tasks, not work items and initiatives. Little to learn before using it.
Enterprise_Features_Review: Team basics are covered. Audit, admin and time tracking sit in the newer Pro layer.
Interface_Flexibility_Review: List, Kanban, table and Gantt views, with little enterprise workflow customisation behind them.
Data_Sovereignty_Review: AGPL core, self-hosted or EU-hosted, with the data under your control either way.
Portability_Review: CalDAV, importers, an API, and a documented move between hosted and self-hosted.
Activity_or_Caveat: Time tracking moved to Vikunja Pro in 2026, out of the free AGPL core.

Name: Wekan
Short_Description: A ten-year-old open-source Trello with swimlanes, checklists, subtasks, colour tags and rule-based automation.
Community_Proxy_Evidence: 21.1k GitHub stars and ten years of continuous releases, marked at Free Software Conference Ukraine in July 2026.
Integration_Notes: A REST API and outgoing webhooks tested against Slack and Rocket.Chat, packaged n8n connectors, and a documented import from Trello.
Deployment: Docker Compose or a snap package, over MongoDB.
Calendar_Sync: An iCalendar feed of card due dates, one way out. No CalDAV.
Data_Out: JSON, CSV and TSV exports; a REST API with outgoing webhooks, and a Trello importer.
Ease_of_Deployment_Review: Compose or a snap package over MongoDB. Meteor upgrades have historically been more eventful than the feature set suggests.
Ease_of_Use_Review: Anyone arriving from Trello is productive immediately, which is the whole proposition.
Enterprise_Features_Review: Board admins, members, commenters and public read-only links, with LDAP and OAuth available.
Interface_Flexibility_Review: Kanban, list, swimlanes and calendar, with rule-based automation behind them.
Data_Sovereignty_Review: MIT throughout, with nothing reserved for a paid edition. Among the cleanest positions here.
Portability_Review: JSON, CSV and TSV exports, a REST API, outgoing webhooks and a documented Trello import.
Activity_or_Caveat: Long-lived and dependable, on a Meteor and MongoDB stack that makes version upgrades the main operational risk rather than the application itself.

Name: Restyaboard
Short_Description: A Trello-shaped board with offline caching, card-level messaging and email-to-card, effectively frozen since 2022.
Community_Proxy_Evidence: 2.1k GitHub stars and no tagged release since 1.7.1 in March 2022. The commercial product continues; the open board does not.
Integration_Notes: A REST API, webhooks and email-to-card. Documented connectors are thin, and none have been refreshed recently.
Deployment: Docker with Nginx, PHP and PostgreSQL.
Calendar_Sync: An iCalendar feed of card due dates, one way out. No CalDAV.
Data_Out: CSV and JSON exports; a REST API with webhooks.
Ease_of_Deployment_Review: Docker with Nginx, PHP and PostgreSQL, against installation documentation that has aged badly.
Ease_of_Use_Review: A competent Trello clone of its era, and it looks precisely like its era.
Enterprise_Features_Review: Organisation admins, board managers and restricted guests. Present, and untouched for years.
Interface_Flexibility_Review: Kanban, list, Gantt and calendar is more views than most boards here offer.
Data_Sovereignty_Review: OSL-3.0 is OSI-approved but unusual, and its reciprocity terms complicate reuse more than MIT or GPL.
Portability_Review: CSV and JSON out with a REST API, which is the part that matters most for a project in this state.
Activity_or_Caveat: Dormant. The last tagged release, 1.7.1, is from March 2022, and nothing in the repository since amounts to a release. Recorded for completeness, not as a recommendation: do not start a deployment here without first checking whether the project has moved.

Name: Titra
Short_Description: Time and task tracking for studios and agencies: assignments, budgets and burn rates against client projects.
Community_Proxy_Evidence: 497 GitHub stars and steady small-team development. A niche tool with a clear audience and little noise around it.
Integration_Notes: A REST API, plus CSV, XLSX and JSON exports aimed squarely at getting time into an accounting system.
Deployment: One container over MongoDB.
Calendar_Sync: None. Neither CalDAV nor an iCalendar feed.
Data_Out: CSV, XLSX and JSON exports; a REST API.
Ease_of_Deployment_Review: One container over MongoDB. Small enough to run and forget.
Ease_of_Use_Review: A time grid and a task list, with very little between you and a filled timesheet.
Enterprise_Features_Review: Project permissions and client rate masking. Enough for an agency, not for a department.
Interface_Flexibility_Review: Narrow on purpose: time grid, task list, project tracking, and no views beyond them.
Data_Sovereignty_Review: AGPL with nothing reserved, and the hosted service is convenience rather than leverage.
Portability_Review: CSV, XLSX and JSON out over a REST API, which is what an accounting handover needs.
Activity_or_Caveat: Small project, narrow remit, and a bus factor to match. It tracks time against tasks well and does not pretend to manage the project around them.

Name: Worklenz
Short_Description: Agency and services-firm workflow: client projects, billable time, task management and reporting.
Community_Proxy_Evidence: Hundreds of forks, moving issues and pull requests, continuing releases, and a smaller ecosystem than the leaders.
Integration_Notes: Modest next to Plane or OpenProject. An API and the commercial roadmap may widen it.
Deployment: Docker Compose with Node.js and PostgreSQL, plus object storage for attachments.
Calendar_Sync: None. Neither CalDAV nor an iCalendar feed.
Data_Out: CSV and Excel exports of tasks, timesheets and reports; REST API.
Ease_of_Deployment_Review: A conventional web stack with a current self-hosting path, and less road behind it.
Ease_of_Use_Review: Planning and timesheets an agency team can pick up without training.
Enterprise_Features_Review: Built for services firms. The enterprise licensing and admin model is still moving.
Interface_Flexibility_Review: Boards, lists, Gantt and reporting, without the workflow extension depth of Redmine or OpenProject.
Data_Sovereignty_Review: The AGPL core self-hosts. Send the business-licence terms to procurement first.
Portability_Review: Ordinary self-hosting with the source available, on a commercial roadmap that may add dependencies.
Activity_or_Caveat: The self-hosted business-licence model and its edition boundaries are still changing.
